title: Subcontractor work lacks acceptance evidence
source_story: User-provided fictional owner stories in this conversation; opening narrative below is a faithful condensed adaptation, not a verbatim transcript.
business_context: Eight internal staff plus regional external service partners.
owner_narrative: We send partners addresses and symptoms by message. Some return detailed reports; others only say done. One replaced a part with branch permission, but head office refused to pay. Assignment time was mistaken for an agreed arrival time during another complaint.

diagnostic_interview.question: Who may approve additional cost?
diagnostic_interview.synthetic_answer: Head office, not the branch contact.
diagnostic_interview.diagnostic_value: Separate site access from spending authority.
diagnostic_interview.branch_if_answer_differs: If detailed instructions were acknowledged and repeatedly ignored, partner performance management may be needed beyond software.

diagnostic_interview.question: What evidence is mandatory?
diagnostic_interview.branch_if_answer_differs: Revise the causal hypothesis and request the corresponding source record; do not reuse this fictional answer for a new customer.

diagnostic_interview.question: Will partners install our application?
diagnostic_interview.synthetic_answer: Most will use a simple phone page but resist another account workflow.
diagnostic_interview.branch_if_answer_differs: Revise the causal hypothesis and request the corresponding source record; do not reuse this fictional answer for a new customer.

evidence.description: A simulated partner invoice includes an unapproved replacement.
A simulated assignment contains no spending limit.
A simulated report says only done.

diagnoses.hypothesis: Delegated work lacks explicit scope, authority, milestones and a completion contract.
diagnoses.counterhypothesis: If detailed instructions were acknowledged and repeatedly ignored, partner performance management may be needed beyond software.
diagnoses.confidence_policy: Qualitative case-world support only; requires fresh customer evidence before reuse.

interventions.process_first: Send a concise work order with scope, escalation contact and evidence requirements; separate technical completion from customer acceptance.
interventions.deterministic_and_assisted_automation: Provide authenticated, job-scoped mobile reporting; record acceptance, agreed window, actual arrival, parts and approval requests.
interventions.rejected_default: Do not replace the whole service platform or deploy autonomous agents solely because the owner reports inefficiency.
interventions.selection_basis: Choose the least complex intervention addressing the supported handoff failure; compare added administration and integration burden.

requirements.statement: Partners can access only assigned jobs.

requirements.statement: Extra spending requires the authorized customer approver.
requirements.rationale: Delegated work lacks explicit scope, authority, milestones and a completion contract.

requirements.statement: Done is not accepted when mandatory evidence is missing.
requirements.rationale: Delegated work lacks explicit scope, authority, milestones and a completion contract.

requirements.statement: Expired access links cannot reveal job data.
requirements.rationale: Delegated work lacks explicit scope, authority, milestones and a completion contract.

acceptance_tests.scenario_and_expected_result: A branch employee cannot approve head-office-only expenditure.
One partner cannot view another partner’s jobs.
Missing evidence creates follow-up rather than fabricated completion.

capability_boundary.proposed_extension: External partner access and spend authorization need separate engineering.
capability_boundary.pricing: No price assigned; current rate card must not be extended by analogy.

evaluation.primary_metric_definition: Partner jobs accepted without documentation rework / completed partner jobs; track unauthorized spend and missed agreed windows.
measurement_cautions: Use a stable denominator and comparable operating periods.
Record missingness and changed case mix.
Do not infer staff reductions from reclaimed task minutes.

implementation.baseline: Collect at least one representative operating cycle before rollout; for monthly billing or maintenance include the relevant full cycle. Extend sampling when volumes or seasonality make the sample unrepresentative.
implementation.scope: Start with one consenting customer group and the staff who own its handoffs; include a normal case and each listed exception.
sequence: Reconcile identities and existing obligations with the process owner.
Run the proposed rules in shadow mode; record disagreements and missed exceptions.
Approve a bounded live pilot only after requirements and exceptions have named owners.
Review outcome metrics, added administrative work and failure logs before expanding.
implementation.simulated_resolution: In this fictional case, MILO introduced the process change: Send a concise work order with scope, escalation contact and evidence requirements; separate technical completion from customer acceptance. The team adopted the proposed workflow for the pilot scope. Routine coordination became explicit; unresolved exceptions continued to require a person.
implementation.simulated_lesson: If detailed instructions were acknowledged and repeatedly ignored, partner performance management may be needed beyond software.
implementation.rollback: Pause automated writes and notifications, retain the event log, export outstanding work and return to a named manual coordinator. Reconcile queued events before resuming to avoid duplicate actions.
implementation.go_no_go: Process owner reviews coverage of acceptance cases, unresolved critical failures, metric direction and staff workload. No fixed performance threshold is claimed without customer agreement.

open_questions: Partner access, payout terms and required evidence must be agreed contractually.
